text.prompt: Make an offering at the Heart Tree
text.rootsBlock: The ancient roots are too thick to pass. They seem to shrink from fire.
text.rootsWither: The roots draw back from your light, and a path opens.
text.needTablets: The great tree does not answer yet. You have not read all five tablets.
text.needOffering: Hold food as an offering, and bring two spirit dust from the restless ones.
text.restored: You lay down your offering with both hands. The old promise is spoken again.

epilogue: The Heart Tree stirs. A warm wind passes through the branches, and the old promise is renewed.
Far along the forest paths, the Neak Ta return to their shrines, and the offerings left for them are honoured once more.
The Ap and Arak grow quiet. The wound that called them begins to close, and the restless ones fade into the dark.
The roots loosen their grip, and the forest opens a little, as if to let you breathe.
The jungle is still deep, still alive, and still wild. You may stay, and keep walking its paths with care.

river.title: The River Road
epilogueUnrestored: The boat slides out from under the trees, and the green walls fall away behind you. The river is wide here, and the sky is larger than you remember.
The forest's wound is still open. The Ap and Arak still wander restless in the dark, and the shrines wait for better days.
You look back once. The canopy hums like something drawing breath, and you feel no shame in leaving.
Someone else may yet walk in, read the stones, and listen. The forest is patient.
The current carries you toward lamplit markets and ordinary mornings. You carry the forest's quiet with you, unfinished.
epilogueRestored: The boat slides out from under the trees, and the river opens wide around you. Behind you the canopy stands calm and unbroken.
The Heart Tree is at peace. The Neak Ta rest at their shrines, and the Ap and Arak have faded into the dark.
You look back once. A warm wind follows the boat to the bend, as if to see you safely off.
The trader poles in easy silence. You have no need to speak.
Downriver, the lamps of the market wait. You carry the forest with you, the way you carry a good memory, and it is light.
